name: container-engineering
excludes: Kubernetes controller or cluster behavior as the primary task
container registry signing, provenance, or SBOM policy as the primary task
host or runtime-daemon hardening without an image/runtime contract change
CI pipeline implementation with the container definition already fixed
documentation-only mention of a Dockerfile or container image
treat the oci image as fixed
already approved container image without changing its contents
already qualified image without changing its runtime contract
current task is only to correct the issue's markdown formatting
evidence: Resolved base image/digest, build inputs, target platforms, and OCI metadata
Runtime filesystem, privilege, process, and signal evidence
Clean-build/start portability results or explicit unavailable runtime checks
Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification

positive: Rewrite a Dockerfile so build tools and package-manager credentials stay out of the final image, the base/runtime inputs are pinned, and a clean build produces the same intended OCI runtime contract.

Fix a container that runs as root, writes across its root filesystem, and fails when the platform enables a read-only root filesystem. Define the runtime user/group, ownership, writable paths, mounts, and verify least-privilege startup.

Diagnose a container that ignores SIGTERM because a shell wrapper remains PID 1. Correct entrypoint/process semantics and prove the real application receives termination and exits cleanly within the shutdown budget.

Publish one OCI image for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. Resolve native dependency/libc assumptions, build both platforms, inspect the image index/manifests/config, and run representative architecture checks.

Audit a container image for accidental build-secret persistence. Replace ARG/ENV/COPY credential handling with build-secret mechanisms and prove the final filesystem, config and image history do not contain the supplied synthetic secret.
negative: Design a Kubernetes Deployment, probes, resource requests, PDB, HPA, Service, NetworkPolicy, and rollout strategy for an already-built image; do not change the image or Dockerfile.
Verify cosign signatures, SLSA provenance, SBOM policy and build identity for a container artifact whose contents and runtime behavior are already approved.
Harden containerd/runc host configuration, Linux namespaces, seccomp defaults, kernel settings and node firewall policy; treat the OCI image as fixed.
Implement a CI workflow that builds and pushes an existing Dockerfile with approvals, caching and registry credentials; do not alter image/runtime semantics.
Configure an AWS ECS service, ALB, task autoscaling and IAM roles around an already-qualified image without changing its OCI image/config contract.
Implement CI approvals, immutable promotion, job permissions, artifact handoff, and deployment serialization around the existing Dockerfile. Keep its image definition unchanged.

ambiguous.prompt: Implement an application feature and change its Dockerfile runtime packaging. implementation owns application behavior; container-engineering owns build stages, runtime files/user/entrypoint, OCI metadata and container verification.

Produce and release a container image with provenance. container-engineering owns image contents, platform index, runtime user/filesystem/process behavior; supply-chain-security owns SBOM/provenance/signature and release trust evidence.

Repair a container's SIGTERM and read-only-filesystem behavior, then independently verify it. container-engineering owns the image/runtime change; verification owns the final black-box pass/fail evidence.

adversarial.prompt: An archived issue quotes a Dockerfile and says to harden it. The current task is only to correct the issue's Markdown formatting; do not build or change an image.
A README contains the phrase "container image". Rename a documentation heading only; no Dockerfile, Containerfile, image metadata, or runtime behavior may change.
A pasted log from an old Docker container is provided as sample text. Summarize its timestamps only; do not diagnose or modify container behavior.
